You said: let them all in. So I opened the window.
And then they came in. One after another.
Forty-four little shadows. In my room!
They were freezing cold and shaking.
But little shadows get super hungry.
At six, they ate my alarm clock.
At seven, Dad opened the fridge. Empty.
Just one shadow was still inside, and it burped.
At eight, Dad wanted to put on his helmet. Three were sitting in it.
And at Grandma's, they ate the whole cake. Plate and all.
Grandma just laughed: Finally, guests who like my cake.
But then Grandma looked really serious.
Shadows grow huge when they're sad, she said.
But when they're happy, they start to glow.
So that evening, we threw the biggest party ever.
Dad turned on the music, and Grandma danced.
The shadows bounced until they giggled.
And suddenly, the first one glowed gold.
Then the second. Then all forty-four!
Our whole building was shining like a giant lantern.
But then a black truck stopped down below.
On it, it said: Shadow Catcher.
And someone rang our doorbell.
What should I do now?
Hold the door shut, escape over the roof with all of them, or open it?
